Import sampling data from the EEA Air Quality Download Service API

Source: R/get_eea_parquet.R
get-parquet.Rd

These functions are wrappers for the 'ParquetFile' endpoints of the European Environment Agency's Air Quality Download Service API.

  • get_eea_parquet_files() downloads a zip file with all the filtered parquet files in it.

  • get_eea_parquet_async() prepares this in the background; the function returns an URL in which the file to be downloaded will be generated.

  • get_eea_parquet_urls() returns a list of URLs corresponding to the filtered parquets. Each parquet file contains the complete time series of a single sampling point, so datetime_start, datetime_end and aggregation_type are ignored.

  • get_eea_summary() estimates the number of files and their size, but does not return any data. Like get_eea_parquet_urls(), it considers complete time series, so datetime_start, datetime_end and aggregation_type are ignored.

  • get_eea_country_city_spos() returns the sampling points in the given countries and cities for the given dataset. Note that it does not filter by pollutants, aggregation_type, datetime_start or datetime_end. To find the sampling points with data for specific pollutants, use get_eea_parquet_urls(), which returns one file per sampling point.

Usage

get_eea_parquet_files(
  countries = "AD",
  cities = NULL,
  pollutants = NULL,
  datetime_start = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1,
  datetime_end = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),
  dataset = 1L,
  aggregation_type = "hour",
  email = NULL,
  compress = TRUE,
  dynamic = TRUE,
  file = tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
)

get_eea_parquet_async(
  countries = "AD",
  cities = NULL,
  pollutants = NULL,
  datetime_start = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1,
  datetime_end = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),
  dataset = 1L,
  aggregation_type = "hour",
  email = NULL,
  compress = TRUE,
  dynamic = TRUE
)

get_eea_parquet_urls(
  countries = "AD",
  cities = NULL,
  pollutants = NULL,
  datetime_start = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1,
  datetime_end = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),
  dataset = 1L,
  aggregation_type = "hour",
  email = NULL
)

get_eea_country_city_spos(
  countries = "AD",
  cities = NULL,
  pollutants = NULL,
  datetime_start = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1,
  datetime_end = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),
  dataset = 1L,
  aggregation_type = "hour",
  email = NULL
)

get_eea_summary(
  countries = "AD",
  cities = NULL,
  pollutants = NULL,
  datetime_start = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1,
  datetime_end = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),
  dataset = 1L,
  aggregation_type = "hour",
  email = NULL
)

Arguments

countries

A vector of country codes from import_eea_countries(). If NULL, data from all countries will be imported.

cities

A vector of cities in the given countries from import_eea_cities(). If NULL, data from all cities in the given countries will be imported.

pollutants

A vector of pollutant notations or IDs from import_eea_pollutants(). If NULL, data for all pollutants will be imported.

datetime_start, datetime_end

Start and end date times, provided as POSIXct, Date or integer R objects.

  • A POSIXct represents an exact instant, and its timezone is respected.

  • A Date represents a whole day; datetime_end includes all of the given day, meaning providing the same Date to each will return a day of data.

  • An integer represents a whole year; datetime_end includes all of the given year, meaning providing the same integer to each will return a year of data.

Note that the EEA reports hourly data in UTC+01, so Date and integer inputs will define days and years in UTC+01 for hourly data, and in the local time of each station for daily data.

dataset

The dataset to use, as a single integer. One of:

  1. Unverified data transmitted continuously (Up-To-Date/UTD/E2a), covering the period not yet covered by verified data.

  2. Verified data (E1a) from 2013 onwards, reported by countries by 30 September each year for the previous year.

  3. Historical Airbase data delivered between 2002 and 2012, before Air Quality Directive 2008/50/EC entered into force. Note that Airbase uses different sampling point identifiers to datasets 1 and 2.

  4. CAMS forecasts, downscaled by the EEA to monitoring stations using a 1x1 km grid. Only available for PM10, PM2.5, O3 and NO2.

  5. Gap-filled E2a, using linear interpolation for smaller gaps, and a regressor based on similar stations for larger ones.

aggregation_type

represents whether the data collected is obtaining the values:

  1. Hourly data ("hour").

  2. Daily data ("day").

  3. Variable intervals (different than the previous observations such as weekly, monthly, etc.) ("var").

email

Optional field to identify the user who make the download and improve the communication if problems are detected.

compress

Boolean value that defines the type of the file to be obtained (TRUE for ZIP or FALSE for parquet). Note that, at the time of writing, the API appears to return a ZIP file regardless of this value.

dynamic

If TRUE, the default, will use the 'dynamic' method, which can combine the results into a single parquet file (in practice, it appears to do so for larger requests only). If FALSE, will use the 'classic' method, which always creates a separate parquet file for each sampling point. The data contained in the files is the same either way, but the dynamic method is typically faster.

file

The file to write the zip file to; should ideally end in ".zip". Defaults to a temporary file using tempfile().

Value

One of:

  • get_eea_parquet_files(): the file argument - the path to the downloaded ZIP file.

  • get_eea_parquet_async(): a path to the URL at which the ZIP file will be made available.

  • get_eea_parquet_urls(): a character vector of URLS to each parquet file.

  • get_eea_summary(): a numeric list, with names numberFiles and size.

  • get_eea_country_city_spos(): a tibble with a single column, localid, containing the local ID of each sampling point (without the country code prefix used in the parquet files).

Details

Arguments which are ignored by a given function are kept for consistency, so that the same arguments can be passed to each of these functions.

Note that cities are defined by the EEA using the 'Urban Audit' city boundaries, which may extend beyond the city's administrative area. For example, "Madrid" includes sampling points in several neighbouring municipalities.
